title: Desolace
body: Desolace is a grey and broken land southwest of Stonetalon, bare rock, bleached bones and brackish pools beneath a stormy sky, green only along the western shore. It is the ancestral home of the centaur, whose holy ground of Maraudon lies hidden in the Valley of Spears, and their clans, the Kolkar, Gelkis, Magram and Maraudine, fight one another across the plains while outsiders dread the day they might unite. The night elves who once lived here are long gone, and the Burning Blade, demons, satyrs and naga have taken their place.

title: Nijel's Point
body: Hidden in the northern mountains, Nijel's Point is a small Alliance camp guarded by soldiers of Stormwind; no one there seems to know who Nijel was. Captain Pentigast's answer to the warring centaur is cold reckoning: united they would be unstoppable, so the Alliance must side with one clan and learn from it how to beat them all. Night elves keep the inn and the roost, and a Darnassian agent searches for two missing children of a merchant house.

title: Ghost Walker Post
body: Ghost Walker Post is a tauren outpost in central Desolace, above the great Kodo Graveyard. From here the Horde deals with the centaur, hoping to ally with one clan against the rest, and fights the Burning Blade. Orgrimmar sent the orc swordsman Takata Steelblade and the Forsaken warlock Maurin Bonesplitter to root out the demons, and the warlock holds the cult's borrowed magic in contempt.

parts.body: Maurin's zeal is not only duty: slaying the demon lord would earn the Warchief's favor, which he means to spend on ends of his own, and he lets the proud Takata believe the hunt is his own plan.

title: Kodo Graveyard
body: South of Ghost Walker Post spreads the Kodo Graveyard, a field of enormous skeletons where aged kodo come to lay themselves to rest, and many of the bones belonged to beasts far larger than any kodo alive. Where death gathers, so do goblins: one buys every bone for furniture and blasting powder, and another tames dying kodo with a device of his own for the Gizelton brothers, whose caravan is the only one brave enough to cross Desolace.

title: Thunder Axe Fortress
body: Thunder Axe Fortress in northern Desolace belongs to the Burning Blade, orcs who have given their loyalty to demons. Within, a red crystal seals the Demon Box that holds the Hand of Iruxos, the relic the cult uses to open portals at Mannoroc Coven, and a seer studies the Sceptre of Light, taken from the naga. Among the fires stands a night elf woman whom the orcs leave be.

parts.body: She is Dalinda Malem of a Darnassian merchant house, the cult's captive, seized with her brother Tyranis and sure she is meant as a sacrifice.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Thunder_Axe_Fortress (stronghold, barracks, cave, watch towers)

parts.body: Tyranis was no captive. He had come to crave arcane power, a crime among his people, and he stood with the cult. His sister called his death terrible, but necessary.

title: Mannoroc Coven
body: Named for the pit lord Mannoroth, Mannoroc Coven lies south of Ghost Walker Post among old night elf ruins, a dead land the demons have blasted further. Burning Blade summoners opened portals here and the Legion came through: infernals, felhounds that hunt mages, nether maidens and doomwarders. Their master is the demon lord Azrethoc, and in a hidden ravine to the east more summoners keep stolen stallions beside the cult's dark steeds.

parts.body: A strip of flayed skin the cultists carry is a pact in an old tongue akin to Eredun, signed by Lord Azrethoc: a demon seeking influence over the Burning Blade itself.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Mannoroc_Coven (named after Mannoroth; night elven ruins; dead land blasted with fel magic; Burning Blade summoned demons through portals)

parts.body: Turned against the portals, the Hand of Iruxos banishes them one by one, and the flood of demons into Desolace is stemmed.

title: Valley of Spears
body: The Valley of Spears in western Desolace belongs to the Maraudine, the clan that guards Maraudon, holy ground where only spirits and the most sacred priests may tread. A war horn on a high bluff calls the clan's warriors. In caves at the valley's end the Nameless Prophet, one of the oldest of all the tribes, communes with the ancestors, and a dryad begs help for her brother, cursed within.

title: Shadowprey Village
body: Shadowprey Village is a Darkspear fishing village on the western coast of Desolace, its docks reaching into the sea and its catch wanted inland at Ghost Walker Post. Tauren keep the inn and the wind riders, one fisherman lives only for revenge on the naga who killed his crew, and the old tauren Roon Wildmane remembers the days he hunted beside the dwarf Hemet Nesingwary.

title: Ethel Rethor
body: On the northwestern coast the ruins of Ethel Rethor lie mostly beneath the waves, a drowned night elf city with one standing tower. From it the Argent Dawn mage Azore Aldamort watches two threats: the Slitherblade naga of Ranazjar Isle, who guard secrets kept for centuries in the Book of the Ancients, and the Burning Blade, said to have taken from the naga the Sceptre of Light, which legend says can sink whole cities beneath the sea.

parts.body: The Sceptre was taken back from the cult's seer and brought to the tower: a grave threat to the world, Azore says, removed from the cult's hands.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Ethel_Rethor (night elven ruin, mostly underwater, lone tower with small bridge; Argent Dawn representative)

parts.body: The Book of the Ancients, called out of the naga's keeping beside the serpent statue of Ranazjar, goes to the Dawn's high council with all the naga's secrets written in it.
